"The settlers want to attack us and force us from our homes," said Moutaz Abdelhadi, 42, a farmer who witnessed the attack in Abu Falah. Partway through the attack, at least two Israeli military jeeps sped through the area, kicking up dust as villagers ran out of their way. The attack continued after the military's arrival, with Israeli soldiers firing tear gas in the direction of the Palestinians who had dodged the jeeps. The sound of live gunfire could be heard in the area, and a Reuters photographer saw at least one armed settler fire a gun. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Palestinian medics said two people were injured and taken to hospitals in the area of Ramallah. One of them was Heidi Levine, a photojournalist with the Washington Post. Video of the attack showed Levine lying on her side on a dirt path with her hands over her face as at least three settlers surrounded her. Speaking from a hospital bed later, Levine, who is in stable condition, said: "I was attacked, pushed to the ground. Luckily I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn't even be here, because they just kept kicking me and kicking me." Levine said the attack ended when her Palestinian colleagues intervened, after which medics rushed her in an ambulance to a clinic in Abu Falah and then to hospital in Ramallah. Her voice shook as she spoke and she had bandages over her left hand. The Washington Post did not immediately respond to a request for comment. SETTLER VIOLENCE HAS SURGED IN WEST BANK Israeli settler violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank has surged, with at least 170 attacks since September 27, around the start of the annual olive harvest, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli settlements monitoring group. The settlers have been emboldened by the right-wing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has overseen a rapid expansion of settlements and smaller outposts across the West Bank. Netanyahu has criticized the violence but has taken few steps to crack down on incidents that have drawn international condemnation and sanction plans by longtime Israeli allies, including Britain. The West Bank is home to some 500,000 settlers and at least 3 million Palestinians. UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law regarding military occupations. Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied. The Abu Falah attack followed a similar attack on Friday morning in the area of Turmus Ayya village, where settlers burned three cars after attacking a group of farmers harvesting olives. The military did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Salah Abu Niswa, who witnessed the attack in Turmus Ayya, said the settlers "snuck up like thieves, they caught someone by himself and began to beat him."

item.title: UK competition regulator targets Microsoft's business software grip
item.description: Britain's competition watchdog proposed designating Microsoft with "strategic market status" in business software, potentially paving the way for interventions in how the US tech major bundles products such as Excel, Teams and its Copilot AI assistant.
item.dc:creator: Paul Sandle, Yadarisa Shabong
item.content:encoded: Britain's competition watchdog proposed designating Microsoft (MSFT.O) with "strategic market status" in business software, potentially paving the way for interventions in how the US tech major bundles products such as Excel, Teams and its Copilot AI assistant. The Competition and Markets Authority launched an investigation in May into whether Microsoft's position in software used by around 20 million people a month in Britain was uncompetitive. On Friday, the regulator said it had found that Microsoft had a strong position in personal computer operating systems and productivity, security, server and database management software, reinforced by barriers customers faced when switching. A Microsoft spokesperson said it did not share the CMA's view. "All our products — including Copilot — are open and interoperable, giving customers the ability to use them alongside competing services," the spokesperson said. AI COMPETITION The CMA said it would investigate whether customers could freely choose AI tools and whether rivals could compete with Copilot. It would also examine whether Microsoft's bundling of security products limited choice and how its licensing practices affected customers' cloud options. CMA Chief Executive Sarah Cardell said business software and cloud services underpinned workplaces across Britain, from small firms to vital public services. "Organisations should be able to choose the products that work best for them, switch provider when they want to and combine services from different suppliers," she said. "We want to ensure businesses have the freedom to choose how they use Microsoft's products alongside alternatives." The regulator will invite views on the proposed designation and will then make a final decision by February. If designated, Microsoft would become the third company subject to Britain's new digital market powers. Alphabet-owned Google (GOOGL.O) was designated in online search, while Google and Apple (AAPL.O) were designated in mobile platforms in October 2025. In June, the CMA [USN:L8N42P0FJ TEXT:"imposed"] new conduct requirements on Google's search services, including allowing publishers to stop their content being used to power the US company's AI features and requiring greater transparency over how its search rankings work. The CMA also said on Friday that Amazon Web Services (AMZN.O) and Microsoft needed to address remaining barriers to switching between cloud providers and using multiple cloud services. Both companies had taken steps to support greater choice, including connecting their data centres with rivals, starting with Google, and removing data transfer fees for customers switching providers. But the CMA said more could be done. The regulator said it would continue working with the companies while keeping the possibility of launching a formal investigation into the cloud sector under review. "We welcome the CMA's acknowledgement that Microsoft's market position in cloud does not justify a Digital Markets Competition Regime designation," a Microsoft spokesperson said. AWS said it also welcomed the update. "We've continued to invest throughout 2026 in new AI, multicloud, and open-standard capabilities that give customers more control over how they build and operate," AWS said.

item.title: Italia prorroga una semana más la suspensión del acuerdo de Schengen con España
item.description: Italia ha prorrogado una semana más la suspensión del acuerdo de libre circulación transfronteriza de la Unión Europea con España a raíz del aumento de las llegadas de migrantes a Ceuta a finales de julio, según informó el viernes una fuente del Gobierno italiano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italia ha prorrogado una semana más la suspensión del acuerdo de libre circulación transfronteriza de la Unión Europea con España a raíz del aumento de las llegadas de migrantes a Ceuta a finales de julio, según informó el viernes una fuente del Gobierno italiano. Un portavoz del Gobierno español dijo que los ministros del Interior de ambos países trabajarían durante la próxima semana para levantar los controles fronterizos. Esta prórroga alinea a Italia con la medida adoptada por Madrid, que ha suspendido sus propios acuerdos de Schengen con Roma hasta el 22 de octubre. Italia suspendió por primera vez el acuerdo de Schengen con España el 31 de julio, en respuesta a una avalancha de más de 72.000 migrantes que cruzaron la frontera desde el vecino Marruecos hacia el enclave español de Ceuta, en el norte de África, y ha prolongado la medida en repetidas ocasiones. Madrid calificó las acciones de Italia de "injustas, contrarias a los intereses de la UE, y discriminatorias para la población española". El portavoz del Gobierno español dijo que las próximas conversaciones entre los ministros del Interior se producen tras un diálogo entre el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, y su homóloga italiana, Giorgia Meloni, al margen de la cumbre del Consejo Europeo celebrada esta semana. La fuente del Gobierno italiano se limitó a indicar que, en los próximos días, los ministros estudiarían formas alternativas de cooperación entre ambos países.

item.title: BOJ chief vows to keep raising rates, anchor inflation around target
item.description: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Friday the central bank will focus on anchoring underlying inflation around its 2% target and won't tolerate any overshoot, stressing anew its resolve to continue raising interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Friday the central bank will focus on anchoring underlying inflation around its 2% target and won't tolerate any overshoot, stressing anew its resolve to continue raising interest rates. Ueda also said recent domestic data and discussions he had held with global policymakers at this week's IMF meetings suggested that economic and price developments were moving roughly in line with the central bank's projections. "As underlying inflation is roughly near our 2% target, we cannot tolerate inflation from accelerating further," Ueda told a news conference in Bangkok. "Our stance has shifted recently to a phase where anchoring inflation around our 2% target has become our big policy objective." The remarks came ahead of the BOJ's key policy meeting later this month, where the board will produce fresh quarterly growth and inflation forecasts that will be scrutinised for clues on the pace and timing of future rate hikes. "As underlying inflation is quite close to 2%, it is becoming more important than before to anchor it around our target," Ueda said, adding that the bank would consider this at its next policy meeting. Ueda will take home insights from his discussions with G7 and G20 colleagues in Bangkok, including what his US counterpart [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"Kevin Warsh"] described as the "common challenge" for global policymakers of dealing with inflation. The BOJ may face renewed pressure to increase the pace of rate hikes amid global inflationary pressures from the Iran war and an AI-driven demand shock, which dominated discussions at this week's IMF meetings. Having raised interest rates in September, many in the BOJ prefer to stand pat at its October 29-30 meeting to await more data on how its hikes so far have affected economic and financial conditions, [USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"sources have told Reuters"]. Even so, the BOJ is likely to drop hawkish signals on the policy outlook that leave scope for a December hike, with analysts noting that AI is adding to the inflationary pressures coming from high energy costs and rising import prices due to a weak yen. "Having discussed with policymakers across the globe, I didn't get the impression their views diverged widely from ours," Ueda said on global inflationary pressures. "But I felt that more policymakers saw global AI demand as somewhat stronger than what the BOJ had expected," he added. UPSIDE RISKS TO INFLATION During this week's annual meetings, the International Monetary Fund highlighted the [USN:L1N45X05U TEXT:"resilience"] of the global economy to shocks such as the Middle East war, with the pain mitigated by brisk AI-related demand. Global policymakers, however, also warned of the inflationary pressure from the AI boom that could warrant further monetary tightening — a message particularly relevant to the BOJ given its still-low borrowing costs. Such discussions may affect the BOJ's new quarterly growth and inflation projections due out at this month's rate review. Already, the BOJ has pivoted away from its cautious approach towards a policy more focused on combatting inflationary risks by hiking rates in June and September. But at 1.25%, its policy rate still means real borrowing costs are negative with inflation hovering around its 2% target and seen accelerating as firms pass on input costs to households. US Treasury Under Secretary [USN:P8N3W600D TEXT:"Erin Browne"] kept pressure on the BOJ to continue tightening to prevent disorderly yen falls, saying on Friday that Japan must adjust its monetary policy to reflect that it no longer faces a deflationary environment. The US Federal Reserve's rate decision at its October 27-28 meeting could also affect the BOJ's debate through any impact on the yen, as the still-wide US-Japan rate divergence has caused the currency to weaken and increased import costs, analysts say.

item.title: Italy prolongs Schengen suspension with Spain, talks loom
item.description: Italy has extended by another week its suspension of the European Union's border-free travel arrangements with Spain over a surge in migrant arrivals in Ceuta in late July, an Italian government source said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy has extended by another week its suspension of the European Union's border-free travel arrangements with Spain over a surge in migrant arrivals in Ceuta in late July, an Italian government source said on Friday. A Spanish government spokesperson said the interior ministers of both countries would work over the coming week on lifting the border controls. The latest extension by Italy aligns with the countermeasure taken by Madrid, which recently extended its own Schengen suspension with Rome until October 22. Italy first suspended Schengen arrangements with Spain on July 31, in response to a [USN:L1N43X0ZO TEXT:"border rush"] by more than 72,000 migrants into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco, and has repeatedly [USN:S8N3RN04D TEXT:"prolonged"] the measure. Rome has argued the presence of thousands of illegal migrants in the Spanish territory posed significant risks to internal security and represented a potential threat of terrorist infiltration. Madrid has described Italy's actions as "[USN:L8N4440UI TEXT:"unjust"], contrary to European Union interests, and discriminatory to the population of Spain". The Spanish government spokesperson said the upcoming talks between the interior ministers followed a conversation between Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and his Italian counterpart Giorgia Meloni on the sidelines of the European Council summit this week. The Italian government source said only that the ministers would in the coming days explore alternative forms of cooperation between the two countries.

item.title: Zelenskiy blasts Trump's diesel deal and calls Russian peace moves a 'parody'
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskiy welcomed the prospect of European allies stepping up their role in talks.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Gray, Yuliia Dysa, Max Hunder
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy took aim on Friday at US President Donald Trump's diesel deal with Russia and welcomed the prospect of European allies stepping up their role in talks, calling Moscow's stance a "parody" of peace negotiations. At a European Union summit in Brussels, Zelenskiy said Russia did not want peace. He added that Ukraine was still experiencing disruptions to [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"the SpaceX Starshield satellite system"] used for battlefield operations and to down Russian drones attacking cities far from the frontline. EU leaders rallied around Zelenskiy after Trump [USN:L1N46203J TEXT:"again criticised"] Ukraine, calling its strikes on Russian refineries a "disgrace". On arriving at the summit, Zelenskiy pointedly referred to his counterparts there as "real leaders". The EU is hosting Zelenskiy at one of the most difficult moments for Ukraine, with missiles and drones raining down on Ukrainian cities and fears that the US could pull back intelligence sharing and weapons support from Kyiv. 'MONEY IN PUTIN'S POCKET' Trump blindsided Zelenskiy last weekend by announcing that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to target each other's energy facilities. Facing US [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"] in November, Trump has blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for pushing up energy prices that could cost him at the ballot box. His [USN:L8N4610WB TEXT:"diesel deal with Russia"] angered Ukraine and European allies. "And now we can see how cash will start flowing back into Russia through the diesel deal," Zelenskiy told a press conference on the sidelines of the summit. "This diesel deal will never be enough to offset the impact of the Strait of Hormuz on global markets. But it will put more money straight into Putin’s pocket to fund this war." Zelenskiy also accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of not being interested in peace talks in any form. "Putin does not want peace talks at the moment, in any form," he said. "He’s playing with words, claiming they respond... Quite simply, it looks like a parody of a genuine desire to end the war." The Kremlin said last week that Ukraine had undermined the possibility of an immediate resumption of peace talks after it had hit Moscow with drones during last month's election. Meanwhile in the latest attacks in Ukraine, Russian [USN:L1N4620A4 TEXT:"drone strikes"] on the city of Kharkiv killed three people, while strikes elsewhere left hundreds of thousands of people without power. In an [USN:L6N4620I6 TEXT:"interview"], Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal told Reuters that the EU would probably have to provide a new loan to Ukraine to help cover its budget gap for next year. “Last winter was already hell, this one will be once again like hell,” Michal said. "We have a lot of gaps to fill, and this is a European mission to fill the gaps that Ukraine needs. Because always, at the start (and) at the end of every conversation, people need to be reminded that we are sitting in a warm room, lights are on, heating is on, the coffee is warm, and we cannot get tired of the war in Ukraine, because they are fighting ... for us." NO READY-MADE EUROPEAN ALTERNATIVE TO STARLINK Ukraine's leadership has been alarmed by disruptions to [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"the Starshield satellite system"]. A source in Ukraine's defence ministry said on Thursday that Starshield receptors were only working at speeds of up to 100 miles per hour (160 kph), complicating their use for military missions. A US official has denied that Trump ordered a deliberate slowdown of Starshield, which is the military-grade version of the Starlink service run by Elon Musk's SpaceX, and Trump said this week intelligence sharing with Ukraine continued. Europe [USN:L6N460141 TEXT:"does not have"] a ready-made alternative to Starlink, although European governments and companies are working on long-term options. Zelenskiy said the operation of SpaceX's satellite communications had improved but had not yet been fully restored, adding that the disruption placed civilian lives at risk. "Starlink is really necessary for Ukraine. And unfortunately, in short term, Europe can't replace this capability," said the EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas. Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery after Zelenskiy declared that Kyiv was [USN:L6N4610BB TEXT:"abandoning the energy ceasefire"] that Trump had announced. "All he's doing is making the world oil price higher. Well, I think that's a disgrace," Trump said in an interview with the Newsmax news outlet. While EU leaders hit out at the US deal to buy Russian diesel, they are also grappling with how to tackle energy prices that have soared since the Iran war, exposing [USN:L1N46107Z TEXT:"divisions"] between member states on day one of the summit on Thursday. "The war will cost €155 billion next year. And we need at least €70 billion more from you – for defence, for weapons, and for our resilience," Zelenskiy said in his address to the EU leaders, which he later posted on X. "This is a realistic amount. And I ask you to find this support. It will help us hold Russia back."

item.title: Major delays at Italian airports due to data network failure
item.description: Air travellers faced delays and cancellations across Italy on Friday due to a technical fault affecting air traffic control, which authorities said was not caused by malicious activity.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Air travellers faced delays and cancellations across Italy on Friday due to a technical fault affecting air traffic control, which authorities said was not caused by malicious activity. Air traffic authority ENAV (ENAV.MI) said it introduced temporary restrictions on air traffic capacity after detecting anomalies overnight on the data transmission network supporting air traffic control services nationwide. As of around 1000 GMT, aviation analytics company Cirium counted 192 cancellations, and found that only around 31% of flights from Italian airports had departed on time, falling to 25% at Milan's Malpensa and 28% at Rome's Fiumicino. ENAV said it had managed to restore 75% of airports' operational capacity using a secondary satellite network and was still working with suppliers to restore the full functionality of the primary data network. Rome airports operator ADR said that "due to technical issues affecting air traffic control systems nationwide, flight delays and cancellations may occur", and advised passengers to contact their airline. Milan airports company SEA issued a similar notice, and separately added that a 24-hour strike by cabin staff at low-cost airline EasyJet (EZJ.L) could cause further travel disruptions.

item.title: Indian police detain 'cockroach' movement founder Dipke ahead of protest
item.description: Police detained Abhijeet Dipke and some supporters ahead of a protest called by him in Delhi's central business district.
item.dc:creator: Sakshi Dayal, Saurabh Sharma
item.content:encoded: Police detained India's 'cockroach' movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and some supporters on Friday, ahead of a protest called by him in capital Delhi's central business district, the latest rally to demand the resignation of India's election chief. The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), opposition groups, and student organisations have held almost daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner [USN:P8N44T0DC TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar's"] resignation over a [USN:L1N45V037 TEXT:"revision of voter lists"] that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision but the Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. Dipke called Friday's protest in support of [USN:L6N46006T TEXT:"two CJP leaders"] detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban. The group and left-wing student organisations had urged supporters to gather at the Central Park in New Delhi's busy Connaught Place shopping and food district on Friday evening to wave and hoist the national flag. POLICE SAY THEY WARNED MOVEMENT LEADER AGAINST PROTESTING The live video on CJP's Instagram handle showed Dipke coming out of a house and walking towards the street, where police officers stopped him and, after a brief argument, hauled him into a police car and drove away. "We are detaining you right now," a police officer could be heard telling Dipke. "I have not broken any law right now ... how can you detain me?" Dipke asked the police officers as he was taken away, the second time in a week that he has been detained. There was no immediate comment from the police on the detention. "Abhijeet is detained by Delhi Police," CJP posted on X. "This government is so scared of the youth waving national flag." Student activist [USN:L4N45X011 TEXT:"Neha Bora"], a prominent face of the protests, was also detained as she tried to reach Connaught Place with dozens of supporters, local media reported. Earlier on Friday, police met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest. Security was stepped up and the park itself shut by civic authorities. Senior police officer Sachin Sharma told news agency ANI that Dipke was served a notice that asked him to obey the law, and that he was informed of the implications of any violations. Television images showed dozens of people arriving at Connaught Place amid heavy security, some of them waving small versions of the national flag. Small protests were also held in financial capital Mumbai and tech hub Bengaluru, while student organisations held a demonstration in the eastern city of Patna, with people waving flags of their organisations and pushing against police barricades. YOUTH USED AS PAWNS, BJP SAYS The cockroach movement has emerged as one of the [USN:L6N46206J TEXT:"biggest political challenge"]s faced by Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power. A [USN:L1N43R02E TEXT:"weeks-long sit-in"] by its supporters earlier this year forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over exam paper leaks. The latest demonstrations erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar's two deputies raised concerns internally about voter list changes, registration procedures and digital systems. The 130 million names that were removed from voter lists starting last year — equivalent to more than the population of Japan — included 28 million people who had died, 63 million who relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced, according to the Election Commission. Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affect Muslims and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, allegations the commission and the BJP reject. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said the demonstrations were the main opposition Congress party's attempt to "seize power". "Instead of channelling the energy of the youth toward nation-building, they are being used as pawns in the politics of anarchy," he said at a media briefing on Friday.

item.title: Rauchen für den Haushalt - Tabaksteuer wird deutlich erhöht
item.description: Rauchen wird in den nächsten Jahren deutlich teurer. Das beschloss der Bundestag am späten Donnerstagabend mit den Stimmen der regierungstragenden Fraktionen von Union und SPD. Am Freitag passierte das Gesetz dann den Bundesrat. Der Preis für eine Packung mit 20 Zigaretten soll damit Anfang 2027 im Schnitt auf 8,77 Euro steigen. Für 2028 sind dann 9,56 Euro geplant, 2029 schon 10,42 Euro und 2030 gar 11,36 Euro. Auch für geschnittenen Tabak und Liquids für E-Zigaretten wird die Steuer erhöht. Gleiches gilt für Zigarren, Zigarillos sowie Pfeifen- und Shisha-Tabak - hier greift die Anhebung allerdings erst ab März 2027.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rauchen wird in den nächsten Jahren deutlich teurer. Das beschloss der Bundestag am späten Donnerstagabend mit den Stimmen der regierungstragenden Fraktionen von Union und SPD. Am Freitag passierte das Gesetz dann den Bundesrat. Der Preis für eine Packung mit 20 Zigaretten soll damit Anfang 2027 im Schnitt auf 8,77 Euro steigen. Für 2028 sind dann 9,56 Euro geplant, 2029 schon 10,42 Euro und 2030 gar 11,36 Euro. Auch für geschnittenen Tabak und Liquids für E-Zigaretten wird die Steuer erhöht. Gleiches gilt für Zigarren, Zigarillos sowie Pfeifen- und Shisha-Tabak - hier greift die Anhebung allerdings erst ab März 2027. Insgesamt wird laut Gesetzentwurf im Zeitraum 2027 bis 2030 mit steuerlichen Mehreinnahmen des Staates von gut zwölf Milliarden Euro gerechnet. Das Geld kommt ausschließlich dem Bund zugute. Finanzminister Lars Klingbeil (SPD) sagte am Rande der IWF-Herbsttagung in Bangkok, mit den Geldern sollten Löcher im Haushalt gestopft werden. Es gehe aber auch um Gesundheitsschutz. Der Bundestag war mit dem Beschluss deutlich über den ursprünglichen Regierungsentwurf hinausgegangen. Insgesamt wurde dafür gesorgt, dass noch einmal gut 3,3 Milliarden Euro zusätzlich in die Staatskasse gespült werden sollen - 750 Millionen im Jahr 2027, aufsteigend bis zu 872 Millionen 2030. Die schwarz-rote Koalition erhofft sich - ähnlich wie bei der geplanten [USN:L8N4600E0 TEXT:"Zuckersteuer"] auf Getränke - eine Lenkungswirkung, so dass Bürger gesünder leben. Die Opposition beklagte eine weitere finanzielle Belastung der Konsumenten. Außerdem wird befürchtet, dass der Schwarzmarkt dadurch angeschoben wird. Nach Angaben des Deutschen Krebsforschungszentrums sterben hierzulande rund 130.000 Menschen pro Jahr an den Folgen des Rauchens. Die volkswirtschaftlichen Kosten und die Belastungen für die Sozialsysteme werden auf rund 100 Milliarden Euro pro Jahr geschätzt.

item.title: European stocks rise, dollar set for weekly loss after yields drop
item.description: European stocks rose on Friday as markets stabilised after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Howcroft
item.content:encoded: European stocks rose on Friday as markets stabilised after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss. Markets have been [USN:L1N46113N TEXT:"rattled"] this week by concerns over higher interest rates and the debt-fuelled financing behind the AI boom, triggering a selloff in technology and chip stocks. Traders increased bets on further US rate hikes after [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"stronger-than-expected"] inflation data on Wednesday, while investors piled into Treasuries and other government bonds. [USN:L1N462067 TEXT:"Asian stocks"] mostly rose and bond markets steadied on Friday, with investors reversing some of the previous session's moves. Indonesian equities suffered their [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"biggest drop since 1998"] after index provider MSCI said the country's market no longer merited emerging market status and outlined plans to remove it from key indexes tracked by funds. Turkey's main stock index also slid [USN:L6N4620AO TEXT:"more than 3%"] after MSCI froze certain changes to its Turkey equity indexes. At 1055 GMT, the MSCI World Equity Index was up 0.4% but still set for a weekly loss (.MIWD00000PUS) . European stock indexes, [USN:L1N461090 TEXT:"hit less hard"] by Thursday's selloff, were higher, with the STOXX 600 up 0.6% (.STOXX) , Germany's DAX up around 1% (.GDAXI) and France's CAC 40 up 0.5% (.FCHI) . London's FTSE 100 was up less than 0.1% (.FTSE) . US stock futures also pointed to a recovery on Wall Street, with S&P 500 futures up 0.2% , although Nasdaq futures were still in the red as investors remained worried about mounting [USN:L1N46104Z TEXT:"credit risks"] linked to the AI trade, particularly among heavily indebted data-centre operators such as [USN:L4N4620S8 TEXT:"CoreWeave CRWV.O"], which helped trigger Thursday's selloff. "The question of monetization to me is still the big question that is not fully answered. There are still some doubts about the sustainability of the profits and the margins from some actors in the sector," said Amelie Derambure, a senior multi-asset portfolio manager at Amundi in Paris. Still, Derambure said she remained overweight US equities and expected [USN:L6N461159 TEXT:"earnings"] to be strong enough to limit any market correction. DOLLAR FALLS, BONDS RECOVER The dollar fell 0.4%, leaving the dollar index at 101.65 and on track for its first weekly decline after three weeks of gains, as lower Treasury yields reduced the currency's appeal. Further worries about AI would push the dollar down further, [USN:L1N46204G TEXT:"analysts said"]. The weaker dollar helped lift the euro from its recent 17-month low. It was last up 0.4% at $1.1257 . European government bond yields edged higher on Friday, with Germany's 10-year yield at 3.4355% . Even so, yields remained lower on the week as investors sought the safety of government debt amid concerns about AI-related companies' finances. G7 government bond markets were on course for their strongest weekly performance since late May. The correlation between German bond yields and the STOXX 600 [USN:L6N4620EU TEXT:"turned positive this week"] for the first time since August, suggesting government debt is regaining some of its safe-haven appeal. That relationship weakened this year amid concerns that the war in Iran could fuel inflation and keep borrowing costs higher for longer. Oil prices were mixed, with Brent crude futures at $106.14 a barrel but still headed for a weekly gain amid concerns over Middle East supplies. Attacks around [USN:L1N46201B TEXT:"the Strait of Hormuz"] have surged in the past 10 days. Gold gained support from the weaker dollar, rising to about $4,174.52 an ounce.

item.title: Jenna Ortega plays an artificial friend in need in 'Klara and the Sun'
item.description: In Taika Waititi's "Klara and the Sun", which stars Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams, a robot delivers lessons on humanity.
item.dc:creator: Hanna Rantala
item.content:encoded: In Taika Waititi's "Klara and the Sun", which stars Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams, a robot delivers lessons on humanity. The dystopian drama is based on Nobel Prize-winning author Kazuo Ishiguro's 2021 bestseller of the same name and set in a technologically advanced future, following what one character describes as a third world war triggered by the abuse of the internet. Ortega plays Klara, an outdated model of an Artificial Friend, an android companion whose sell-by date is fast approaching when, to her relief, teenager Josie (Mia Tharia) and her mother (Adams) buy her. Programmed to prevent loneliness, Klara is full of quirks and hopes and believes in the healing power of the sun. Her traits come in handy in a household marked by grief and mystery. "It felt like a very timely story," said Ortega at the movie's world premiere at the London Film Festival on Thursday. "To see it put in a futuristic world and see that we still struggle with the same things and the answer's kind of always in one another and listening to one another, I thought it was a really nuanced, thoughtful way of putting it." Waititi, who directed, co-wrote and produced the movie, was struck by Ishiguro's allegorical interplay between humans, artificial intelligence and nature. "She's a machine who comes into the world of a broken family and somehow teaches them the importance of being human," Waititi said. "It's vital right now because we're now in a moment where we're maybe on the cusp of losing control of our relationship with technology," said Waititi, adding that he also wanted the film to "remind people to put the devices down, not because there's a threat or anything, but just put the thing down because it's a distraction, and just be with the people you're with." While Waititi injected some of his signature humour into the movie, he said he wanted to "keep the profound feeling and the drama from the book". "There's some funny bits there, but it's probably my most dramatic film," Waititi said. "Klara and the Sun", which also stars Natasha Lyonne, Steve Buscemi, Aran Murphy and Rachel House, will go on release globally from October 21.

item.title: Oil heads for weekly gain with focus on Middle East supply
item.description: Oil prices steadied on Friday and were heading for weekly gains on uncertainty over Middle East supplies and a larger-than-expected draw from US crude stockpiles, while European diesel margins dropped after an IEA move to release more of the fuel.
item.dc:creator: Enes Tunagur
item.content:encoded: Oil prices steadied on Friday and were heading for weekly gains on uncertainty over Middle East supplies and a larger-than-expected draw from US crude stockpiles, while European diesel margins dropped after an IEA move to release more of the fuel. Brent crude futures were flat at $105.92 a barrel at 1311 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down 22 cents, or 0.2%, to $97.75. "The relative stability reflects a market caught between persistent supply disruption risks in the Middle East, where attacks on ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue to underpin prices," said Saxo Bank analyst Ole Hansen. WTI settled up more than 3% on Thursday after a big [USN:L6N46115T TEXT:"US crude stock draw"] on hurricane production shut-ins. So far this week, Brent has risen 1.2% and WTI 6.5%. "The IEA's pledge to release the remaining 100 million barrels under its March agreement, together with reports that the US is considering easing sanctions on some dark fleet tankers, may be weighing slightly on sentiment," Hansen said, adding that the International Energy Agency release is unlikely to ease diesel supply tightness. IRAN SAYS IT IS STEPPING UP STRIKES Supply concerns also increased as attacks around [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"the Strait of Hormuz"] surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month. European diesel refining margins fell by nearly 2% on Friday to $78.67 a barrel, after the IEA [USN:L1N4610MY TEXT:"agreed"] on Thursday to release more than 20 million barrels of the fuel to the market. Those margins rose as high as $95 a barrel in September as diesel supply tightened because of wars in Ukraine and Iran. "Intensified Iranian attacks drove Gulf crude flows sharply lower," Kpler analysts said in a report on Thursday, adding that they expected a slower and more uneven recovery in Hormuz flows in the absence of a comprehensive political deal. Washington is considering [USN:L1N461108 TEXT:"lifting"] sanctions on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have carried oil and petroleum products from countries such as Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in a bid to cut record global freight rates. The discussions come days after US President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, a move met with criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some of Trump's fellow Republicans.

item.title: Order to limit Starshield for Ukraine came from inside White House, sources say
item.description: The order to limit a satellite system used by Ukraine for battlefield communications and drone operations came from inside the White House, according to two US officials and a Western official briefed on the matter.
item.dc:creator: Erin Banco, Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: The order to limit a satellite system used by Ukraine for battlefield communications and drone operations came from inside the White House, according to two US officials and a Western official briefed on the matter. The officials said leaders at the Defense Department received a message that the SpaceX Starshield service for the Ukrainian military needed to be slowed. The officials, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, did not specify who in the White House made the decision or who was responsible for implementing the order. The Pentagon is the biggest customer of Starshield, which is the military-grade version of the Starlink service. Ukrainian officials said this week that military-grade Starlink receptors [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"stopped working in Ukraine"] when mounted on fast-moving objects, interfering with the performance of Ukrainian drones that rely on them for onboard guidance systems over Ukrainian territory. A person in Ukraine's Defence Ministry said on Thursday that the receptors were now working when in motion, but only at speeds of up to 100 miles per hour (160 kph). US PRESSURES UKRAINE OVER REFINERY ATTACKS The move to temporarily restrict the vital communications system came as President Donald Trump has pressured Kyiv to stop its attacks on Russian refineries, which he has blamed for the soaring energy prices that are denting his Republican Party's prospects in the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"November midterm elections"]. But experts say that surge in energy costs is mainly the result of the US-Israeli war with Iran , which brought Iranian attacks on energy facilities and has largely shut the vital Strait of Hormuz. In response to a request for comment about the order to limit Starshield, a senior US official said: "No such request was ever made by the president." The White House did not respond to questions about whether other administration officials might have made the request. Starshield was developed by SpaceX specifically for government and national-security customers, particularly the US Department of Defense. Starshield uses the Starlink constellation as its backbone. Ukrainian officials said the restrictions complicated strike missions against Russian forces and logistics in occupied territory and slowed interceptor drones used to shoot down incoming Russian Shahed drones. Elon Musk, the CEO of SpaceX, said on X on Wednesday that because Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government, any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military or the president. SpaceX did not respond to a request for comment. The Department of Defense and the Ukrainian embassy in Washington also did not respond to requests for comment. DECLINE IN RELATIONS Relations between Kyiv and Washington have deteriorated in recent days following a meeting in Miami on October 9 that convened representatives from both countries as well as Europe and the World Bank. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, the Trump administration’s Middle East envoy, struck a tough tone with Ukraine in the meeting, according to a separate person familiar with the matter. They told Ukrainian officials that the US was frustrated with Kyiv's continued strikes on Russian refineries despite repeated requests from Washington to stop. The US delegation also explained Washington's decision to strike a diesel deal with Russia, saying the White House hoped it would [USN:L1N45Y0OS TEXT:"soften Moscow's stance"] on peace talks. That deal, under which Russia will supply more than 2.25 million barrels of diesel to US and global markets, has triggered a backlash from some US lawmakers, who say it will give Moscow cash to pursue its war without forcing Russian President Vladimir Putin to make concessions to end the conflict. In the days that followed, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Trump criticized each other, with Zelenskiy calling the US decision on the Russian diesel deal "weak." Trump called for elections in Ukraine and [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:"Zelenskiy's ouster"]. Behind the scenes, American officials threatened to stop providing intelligence to Kyiv about Russian missile launches that Ukraine uses to thwart attacks, as Reuters previously reported. Trump said on Tuesday Washington was [USN:L1N45Z0GP TEXT:"still sharing intelligence"] with Ukraine. Following the move to restrict Ukraine's access to Starshield, the Ukrainians made calls on Tuesday and Wednesday to find answers from senior officials at the White House, State Department and Pentagon, a senior Ukrainian official said, adding that Kyiv was told it was a White House decision. The Pentagon has spent billions of dollars on the Starlink and Starshield services. It has also bought dedicated Starshield satellites, including communications spacecraft for missile-warning missions and a spy constellation for the National Reconnaissance Office, Reuters reported in 2024.

item.title: Indonesian rescue centre takes in more orangutans as fires rage
item.description: In the jungles of Indonesian Borneo, a rehabilitation centre is taking in more orangutans as the country's worst wildfires in a decade sweep through the forest home of the critically endangered animals.
item.dc:creator: Willy Kurniawan, Yuddy Budiman
item.content:encoded: In the jungles of Indonesian Borneo, a rehabilitation centre is taking in more orangutans as the country's worst wildfires in a decade sweep through the forest home of the critically endangered animals. The intense [USN:L4N44O09W TEXT:"wildfires"], burning mainly on the islands of Borneo and Sumatra, began in July and could continue until November, aggravated by a severe El Niño weather pattern, the government has warned. "I think so far this looks quite similar to the 2015 fires," said Karmele Llano Sanchez, co-founder of Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI), who has worked in Indonesia for more than 20 years. "It's possible that in the months to come, they (the orangutans) will also be affected by not having enough to eat, not having enough room, enough habitat, and starvation." The world's three species of orangutan are native only to Borneo and Sumatra. YIARI, in the Ketapang region of Indonesia's West Kalimantan province, is now looking after 90 orangutans, after rescuing 49 since August, foundation spokesperson Heribertus Suciadi said. Over the last three years, the centre rescued three to five animals a year, he added. The fires and haze have shrouded parts of Borneo, which also includes the Malaysian states of Sarawak and Sabah, in a hazardous smog that has also spread to Singapore and the Malaysian peninsula, forcing some schools to close and causing a spike in respiratory illnesses. Sampurna, an orangutan that [USN:L1N44R01J TEXT:"Reuters encountered"] in August, was found gasping for air and writhing on the ground in a palm oil plantation. Sampurna died on August 30, the forestry ministry said last month. Sanchez, who performed the necropsy on the great ape, said Sampurna died less than 12 hours after being rescued and had very dark lungs owing to respiratory problems, likening them to those of a heavy smoker. From January to July this year, fires burned around 202,000 hectares (500,000 acres) in Indonesia. No official data for subsequent months has been released, but non-governmental organisations estimate fires have burned at least 600,000 hectares more since. In 2015, fires burned nearly 960,000 hectares, forestry ministry data showed. "I think in general, what we see is that these orangutans that were surviving in these fragments of forest, and the forest fragments are becoming smaller and smaller and smaller," Sanchez said. RESCUE MISSIONS Once YIARI volunteers receive reports of orangutan sightings, they use a drone to determine the areas ravaged by the fires and whether orangutans were living there, Heribertus said. Equipped with tranquilisers, rescuers then drive for hours to the burned forest to find the orangutans, sometimes using a net to capture the apes before taking them to safety. The foundation has more than 200 staff, including firefighters and veterinarians. "Fires are occurring in many areas. As a result, the orangutans are being displaced into plantations," said Relly Susanto, a YIARI patroller. On a recent August day at the YIARI centre, orangutans swung through the trees and walked on vines, as youngsters ate fruit next to their mothers. While there is no escape from the smoke even at YIARI, the centre is not currently at risk from the fires themselves and some of the rescued orangutans have been [USN:L4N45X00X TEXT:"returned to the wild"] in safer locations. At the moment, YIARI has enough capacity to take in the orangutans, Sanchez said. But with the fires showing little sign of abating, she is not sure how long that will last. "It's difficult to quantify how many orangutans will need to be rescued," she said. "One of our concerns is whether we'll have enough capacity to really get all of these rescued orangutans into the facility." Click on https://bit.ly/4hWQmeq to see the related photo essay.

item.title: WEF could appoint Lagarde as early as November, sources say
item.description: The World Economic Forum could appoint Christine Lagarde as its next chair as soon as next month, four people close to the organisation told Reuters, meaning she would step down early as European Central Bank chief and trigger a wider reshuffle at the top of the ECB.
item.dc:creator: Dave Graham, Francesco Canepa
item.content:encoded: The World Economic Forum could appoint Christine Lagarde as its next chair as soon as next month, four people close to the organisation told Reuters, meaning she would step down early as European Central Bank chief and trigger a wider reshuffle at the top of the ECB. Lagarde's ECB term is scheduled to end in October 2027. Leaving early would give European Union leaders a chance to pick a new ECB President before France's spring presidential election, which opinion polls suggest the far-right could win, and could pave the way for a deal involving two other senior ECB roles. The WEF's Board of Trustees, which includes Lagarde herself, was due to meet on November 2 and could elect her as its next chair, said the people close to the organisation, who spoke on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter. No final decision has been taken yet, they said. A spokesperson for the WEF said the forum could not confirm when the next full Board of Trustees meeting would take place, but that the aim was to hold one before the end of the year. Two of the people said the board could also set a date for a vote that would enable Lagarde to appear as the designated chair when the WEF's annual meeting takes place in January in Davos, where political and business leaders gather to discuss global economic and financial issues. They cautioned that Lagarde's election was not certain but said the 70-year-old former French finance minister had broad support from the board, which lists 27 members on its website. The ECB declined to comment. FINDING A SUCCESSOR BEFORE THE FRENCH ELECTIONS Either timetable would leave enough time for a new ECB President to clear all the formal hurdles that come with EU appointments well before the end of French President Emmanuel Macron's term in May. Lagarde's desire to give Macron a say on her successor was one factor in the timing, a fifth person said. There is concern in European political circles that negotiations over who takes over from her could become more difficult if far-right leader Marine Le Pen were to win the French presidency. Based in Geneva, the WEF board is currently co-chaired by BlackRock Chief Executive Larry Fink and Roche Vice Chairman Andre Hoffmann, who assumed the role after founder Klaus Schwab stepped down last year. The board also includes public-sector figures such as International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and Jordan's Queen Rania and leading business chiefs like Salesforce's Marc Benioff and Siemens' Jim Hagemann Snabe. Lagarde, who [USN:L1N46002V TEXT:"is attending"] the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok this week, has said she will remain at the ECB until next year but has stopped short of committing to remain until her term formally ends in October. Her exit would open a second vacancy on the ECB's six-member Executive Board after Isabel Schnabel's resignation last month. Chief Economist Philip Lane is meanwhile due to step down in May. EU officials say the three appointments could be agreed as part of a package deal among member states. The former central bank governors of the Netherlands and Spain, Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernandez de Cos, are seen as frontrunners for the presidency, while France is understood to be targeting the chief economist's post. Germany plans to put forward a candidate to replace Schnabel, who heads the ECB's market operations, the people said.

item.title: Tesla's new Roadster turns in air with SpaceX thrusters, won't land until 2028
item.description: Tesla unveiled a redesigned Roadster powered with rocket-style thrusters on Thursday and said it would start production in 2028, more than a decade after it first showed a next-generation version of its electric sports car.
item.dc:creator: Abhirup Roy, Mrinmay Dey
item.content:encoded: Tesla (TSLA.O) unveiled a redesigned Roadster powered with rocket-style thrusters on Thursday and said it would start production in 2028, more than a decade after it first showed a next-generation version of its electric sports car. The white two-seater vehicle, developed in collaboration with CEO Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX, drove upside down on a ramp using a suction system, turned in the air and landed using built-in thrusters. Later in the event it used the thrusters to jump over a truck and other vehicles, twisting in the air during the maneuver. Some watchers saw the collaboration as Musk drumming up interest in a merger of the two big companies he controls, an idea he has explored by discussing their overlap. Tesla shares were up 5% in premarket trading on Friday. The reveal gives Tesla a showpiece car after years of missed Roadster deadlines, but it comes as the company shifts its focus to self-driving technology and robotics, and days before third-quarter results that analysts say matter more to investors. "It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers," Gene Munster, managing partner at Tesla investor Deepwater Asset Management, said on social media platform X. "The Roadster event is the latest example of why Elon can't wait to bring (Tesla) and (SpaceX) together," Munster said. Musk has played down the car's importance to Tesla's finances, describing it in 2023 as a "small potato situation" that would not "move the needle in a major way financially." But the car still carries symbolic weight. "Tesla does not currently have a halo car, or high-performance luxury vehicle designed to showcase an automaker's best engineering and technology. The Roadster will be Tesla's new halo car," Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein said in a note last month. Viewers and witnesses gushed over the spectacle of the launch. "That was the most insane product demo I've ever seen," Tesla fan and investor Sawyer Merritt posted on X. "I just saw this in person, and I'm still asking how this wasn't AI." Musk and other executives did not specify any target prices at Thursday's event, although Tesla nearly a decade ago quoted a base price of $200,000 for the vehicle. Tesla's reservation page for the Roadster after Thursday's event showed a "Performance" version of the vehicle requiring a $50,000 deposit and a "Thrust" version with "acceleration thrusters" requiring a $250,000 deposit. A "Rocket" variant, which Tesla says is "invite only," is described as a single-seat model with a "full flight system." 'HALFWAY TO THE SPEED OF SOUND' The event at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, had all the elements of a classic Musk product reveal: dramatic music, smoke, mechanical hissing sounds and a launch countdown. "This is the culmination of incredible work by Tesla and SpaceX engineers working closely together to make something that you haven't seen in any movie," Musk, wearing a silver Western-style belt buckle emblazoned with the Tesla logo, told a cheering crowd of enthusiasts and investors. The Roadster can accelerate from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in less than one second and can hit a top speed of over 230 mph (370 kph), Tesla vehicle engineering chief Lars Moravy said. "Definitely much faster than that," an excited Musk said. "I think you've got to crack halfway to the speed of sound." The Roadster can also travel over 300 miles (480 km) on a single charge. That is less than half of what Musk promised in 2017, when Tesla first revealed a prototype of the second-generation Roadster and said that deliveries would begin in 2020. The original Roadster, released in 2008 and on sale until 2012, was Tesla's first-ever electric vehicle and used a Lotus Elise chassis. It helped change the world's view of what an EV could be. The company has since been known for its Model Y and Model X SUVs and Model S and Model 3 sedans. The reveal of the second-generation Roadster comes amid a sharp shift in Tesla's focus to artificial intelligence-led self-driving tech and robotics, from manufacturing cars for human drivers. This year, Tesla stopped selling Model S and X vehicles to make space for production of its Optimus humanoid robots. It also launched Cybercab — a two-seater robotaxi that comes without manual controls such as a steering wheel, pedals and mirrors. Tesla is set to report third-quarter results on October 21. Sales of Tesla's aging lineup of EVs have declined over the past two years, although high gas prices helped boost deliveries in the third quarter. "The margin and cash flow numbers will carry far more weight with investors than anything they saw at the reveal," said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst for Asia-Pacific at trading platform eToro.

item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: L'Europe tire parti des bons résultats du T3 après l'accalmie dans la "tech"
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Europe tire parti des bons résultats du T3 après l'accalmie dans la "tech" 16 octobre (Reuters) - Wall Street est attendue sur une hausse prudente et les Bourses européennes avancent vendredi à mi-séance, les résultats des entreprises étant bien accueillis et les signes d'une accalmie dans le secteur technologique redonnant confiance aux investisseurs. UniCredit autorisé par la BCE à prendre le contrôle de Commerzbank MILAN, 15 octobre (Reuters) - UniCredit a obtenu l'autorisation de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) pour prendre le contrôle de Commerzbank, a annoncé jeudi soir la banque italienne, alors que son offre publique d'achat hostile a porté sa participation dans son concurrent allemand à 48%. FMI: L'Europe doit stimuler la croissance ou emprunter moins pour garantir la viabilité de sa dette BANGKOK, 16 octobre (Reuters) - L'Europe doit croître plus rapidement ou emprunter moins pour maintenir sa dette sur une trajectoire viable, a déclaré vendredi le Fonds monétaire international (FMI), soulignant que les plans de redressement prévus pourraient ne pas être suffisants. UBS étudie des options à l'étranger au cas la réglementation suisse devient insupportable à ses yeux selon des sources ZURICH, 16 octobre (Reuters) - UBS étudie différents scénarios, dont un déménagement de son siège social ou une fusion avec une autre banque, au cas où la Suisse adopterait de nouvelles règles bancaires que le groupe jugerait excessivement strictes, selon trois sources proches du dossier. Schneider relève ses objectifs 2026 après un T3 record porté par les centres de données 16 octobre (Reuters) - Schneider Electric a relevé vendredi pour la deuxième fois de l’année ses objectifs de résultat d'exploitation et de chiffre d’affaires 2026, porté par la demande des géants du cloud pour les centres de données dédiés à l’intelligence artificielle. Christine Lagarde pourrait être nommée présidente du Forum de Davos dès novembre-sources ZURICH/BANGKOK, 15 octobre (Reuters) - Le Forum économique mondial (WEF) pourrait nommer Christine Lagarde à sa présidence dès novembre, ont déclaré à Reuters quatre sources proches de l'organisation, ce qui impliquerait un départ anticipé de ses fonctions à la tête de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE). L’AIE va accélérer la mise sur le marché des stocks de pétrole, dont plus de 20 millions de barils de diesel PARIS, 15 octobre (Reuters) - L’Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE) est convenue jeudi de mettre sur le marché plus de 20 millions de barils de diesel dès que possible, ainsi que les volumes restants des réserves d’urgence libérées en mars, afin de contribuer à approvisionner le marché et à freiner la flambée des prix. États-Unis: Les prix à la production enregistrent en septembre leur plus forte hausse en quatre ans et demi 15 octobre (Reuters) - Les prix à la production (PPI) aux États-Unis ont enregistré en septembre leur plus forte hausse en quatre ans et demi, sous l'effet de l'augmentation des coûts des biens et des services, dernier signe en date d'un élargissement des pressions inflationnistes au-delà des produits énergétiques. États-Unis: Les ventes au détail augmentent plus que prévu en septembre avec les prix de l'essence Les ventes au détail aux Etats-Unis ont augmenté plus que prévu en septembre, portées par la hausse des prix de l'essence, même si les dépenses dans d'autres secteurs sont restées modérées, montrent les données publiées jeudi par le département du Commerce. Alstom prolonge de 15 ans son contrat avec Greater Anglia pour 800 millions de livres sterling 15 octobre (Reuters) - Alstom a annoncé jeudi avoir signé une prolongation de 15 ans de son contrat de maintenance avec l’opérateur ferroviaire britannique Greater Anglia, pour un montant d’environ 800 millions de livres sterling (946,38 millions d'euros).

item.title: OFRMO Summary
item.description: L'Iran exporte du GPL et du kérosène malgré le blocus américain, selon des données
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Iran exporte du GPL et du kérosène malgré le blocus américain, selon des données DAMAS/LONDRES, 16 octobre (Reuters) - L’Iran a réussi à exporter quelques cargaisons de gaz de pétrole liquéfié (GPL) et de kérosène depuis juillet, malgré le blocus naval américain, selon des données de suivi du trafic maritime et des sources spécialisées dans la sécurité. USA: Une fusillade dans une école de l'Oregon fait quatre morts, le tireur abattu 15 octobre (Reuters) - Un adolescent de 16 ans a ouvert le feu jeudi dans une école primaire de Bend, dans l'Oregon, faisant quatre morts, dont trois enfants, avant d'être abattu par une personne qui l'avait poursuivi dans l'établissement, a annoncé la police. Attaques de drones russes sur plusieurs villes, dont Kharkiv, au moins trois morts 16 octobre (Reuters) - - Des attaques de drones russes ont fait au moins trois morts vendredi en Ukraine, deux à Kharkiv, la deuxième ville du pays, et un dans la région de Volyn (nord-ouest), ont rapporté les autorités. L'Ukraine dispose de réserves de gaz au plus haut niveau depuis 2020, selon le DG de Naftogaz KYIV, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Le directeur général par intérim de Naftogaz, la société publique ukrainienne du pétrole et du gaz, a dit à Reuters que l'entreprise avait constitué ses plus importantes réserves de gaz depuis six ans en prévision de l'hiver, malgré une recrudescence des frappes russes sur ses installations. L'UE fait bloc autour de Zelensky face aux ruptures à répétition de Trump BRUXELLES/KYIV, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Les dirigeants de l'Union européenne ont fait bloc vendredi derrière le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky, fragilisé par le "lâchage" de Donald Trump, qui met en péril l'appareil de défense de l'Ukraine face aux incessantes frappes russes. La Chine est prête à coopérer avec l'UE pour remédier aux déséquilibres mondiaux PÉKIN, 16 octobre (Reuters) - La Chine est prête à engager un dialogue avec l'Union européenne (UE) pour améliorer la communication sur certains aspects de la gouvernance économique mondiale et de la coordination des politiques macroéconomiques, a déclaré vendredi le ministre chinois des Finances. La reprise des frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes est une "honte", dit Trump 16 octobre (Reuters) - La reprise des frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes est une "honte" qui maintient les prix mondiaux de l'énergie à un niveau élevé, a déclaré le président américain Donald Trump à la chaîne Newsmax lors d'une interview diffusée jeudi. Ukraine : La décision de limiter le réseau Starshield a été prise à la Maison blanche selon des sources NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, 15 octobre (Reuters) - L'ordre de limiter l'utilisation du réseau de satellites à usage militaire Starshield, développé par SpaceX, utilisé par l'Ukraine est venu de la Maison blanche, selon deux responsables américains et un responsable occidental au fait de la question. Lula promet la gratuité des transports en commun le week-end BRASILIA, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Le président brésilien Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a déclaré jeudi qu'il allait soumettre au Parlement un amendement constitutionnel garantissant la gratuité des transports publics le week-end, une nouvelle mesure à destination des revenus modestes avant le deuxième tour de l'élection présidentielle. La nouvelle porte-parole de la Maison Blanche admet avoir échoué l'examen du barreau WASHINGTON, 16 octobre (Reuters) - La nouvelle porte-parole de la Maison blanche, Katie Zacharia, a déclaré jeudi soir qu'elle n'avait pas réussi l'examen du barreau, ce qui, selon la plupart des experts juridiques, lui interdit de prétendre au titre d'avocate alors qu'elle s'est initialement présentée comme telle.

item.description: France et Allemagne d'accord sur un plan pour l'automobile
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France et Allemagne d'accord sur un plan pour l'automobile PARIS/BERLIN, 16 octobre (Reuters) - La France et l'Allemagne ont annoncé vendredi un accord sur une "approche commune" visant à garantir l'avenir de l'industrie automobile européenne, avec un accent mis à la fois sur la transition énergétique et sur une production des véhicules en Europe. Une étoile verte récemment découverte émerveille les astronomes WASHINGTON, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Pour la première fois, des astronomes ont identifié une étoile verte, un vestige stellaire dense appelé "naine blanche", qui a pris une teinte fantomatique de vert chartreuse après avoir absorbé des débris rocheux provenant de planètes qui, autrefois, gravitaient autour d’elle. La santé du pape Léon en "amélioration constante", dit le Vatican CITÉ DU VATICAN, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Le pape Léon XIV continue de se remettre de son intervention chirurgicale subie mardi pour un nodule cancéreux au poumon, a déclaré vendredi le Vatican, soulignant "l'amélioration constante" de son état de santé. Le pape Léon XIV se rétablit comme prévu de son opération d'un cancer du poumon CITÉ DU VATICAN, 15 octobre (Reuters) - - Le rétablissement du pape Léon XIV de son opération d'un cancer du poumon suit son cours, a annoncé jeudi le Vatican, qui précise que le souverain pontife de 71 ans a recommencé à travailler. Les dirigeants de l'UE se réunissent en sommet, tensions en vue sur le budget Les chefs d'Etat et de gouvernement de l'Union européenne se réunissent jeudi à Bruxelles pour un sommet lors duquel devraient être mises en exergue les divergences sur l'ampleur du prochain budget pluriannuel et sur les priorités de dépense du bloc communautaire, sans accord attendu dans l'immédiat. Macron va effectuer une tournée dans le Golfe, sécurité et énergie au menu Emmanuel Macron effectuera en début de semaine prochaine une tournée dans le Golfe afin de "poursuivre sa mobilisation" auprès de dirigeants régionaux pour revenir à la stabilité et à la libre circulation dans le détroit d'Ormuz, voie cruciale pour les livraisons énergétiques mondiales, a dit mercredi l'Elysée. Albanie: Le Premier ministre exclut de démissionner face aux manifestations étudiantes Le Premier ministre albanais Edi Rama a exclu de démissionner jeudi auprès de Reuters, alors que le pays est secoué par des manifestations étudiantes émaillées de violences. Mélenchon présente un programme budgétaire censé réduire la dette de 25 milliards d'euros Le candidat de La France insoumise (LFI) à l'élection présidentielle, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, a présenté mercredi une feuille de route budgétaire prévoyant plus de 106 milliards d'euros de recettes, 82 milliards de dépenses et une réduction de la dette publique de 25 milliards. Albanie: Manifestations étudiantes, incendie au ministère de l'Education Un incendie s'est déclaré mercredi au sein du ministère albanais de l'Education, à Tirana, en marge de manifestations étudiantes émaillées de violences et de heurts avec les forces de l'ordre, qui ont fait usage de gaz lacrymogène et de canons à eau pour disperser les manifestants. Le ministre polonais des Affaires étrangères demande à Musk s'il se livre à des manœuvres politiques avec Starlink en Ukraine Le ministre polonais des Affaires étrangères Radosław Sikorski a demandé mercredi à Elon Musk s’il "faisait de la politique" avec Starlink en Ukraine, après que Kiev eut déclaré que SpaceX avait imposé une limitation sur certains services, perturbant ainsi les missions des drones de combat.
